headline: High: LangGraph’s broad write/network orchestration can drive pdf.js into unsafe downstream actions; shared state also creates medium leakage and conflict risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LangGraph can ingest outputs from developer-defined tools and persist shared graph state; pdf.js processes PDF content in a browser-based worker. If a PDF contains instruction-like text and LangGraph later treats extracted content as trusted input, prompt injection is plausible. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF LangGraph nodes pass PDF-extracted text into an LLM prompt without provenance tagging
IF the PDF content is copied from pdf.js output into LangGraph tool inputs
mitigations: Add explicit provenance labels to all PDF-derived text
Insert a human review step before any instruction-following action
Strip or escape prompt-like delimiters from extracted text
Use separate channels for data and instructions
requires-engineering: enforce schema-validated message passing between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: LangGraph can read/write application-defined files and handle model-provider API keys, while pdf.js reads PDF files in a browser context. If both operate on the same workspace, PDF contents can flow into LangGraph outputs or logs. pdf.js itself has no network egress, so the main leakage path is shared storage rather than uncontrolled exfiltration.
conditions: IF both agents share the same filesystem or workspace
IF LangGraph logs or forwards PDF contents into model-provider requests
mitigations: Place pdf.js and LangGraph in separate workspaces
Disable logging of raw document text
Restrict LangGraph to metadata-only reads where possible
Rotate any exposed API keys after testing
requires-engineering: add workspace-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LangGraph has broad filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and network egress capabilities; pdf.js is browser-based and can read PDF files. They do not both show unrestricted write to the same directory, but LangGraph’s shared checkpointer state can still conflict with concurrent instances or with files produced by pdf.js. The overlap is real, though not the high-severity same-dir write case.
conditions: IF LangGraph instances share the same checkpointer backend without locking
IF pdf.js writes PDFs into a directory LangGraph also mutates
mitigations: Use per-run namespaces in the checkpointer
Avoid concurrent writes to shared artifacts
Keep pdf.js outputs read-only for LangGraph
Add file-locking around shared state
requires-engineering: implement optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph is an orchestration framework that can execute downstream tools, while pdf.js extracts document content. If LangGraph treats pdf.js output as authoritative, it can trigger irreversible actions such as sending messages, writing files, or invoking APIs based on unverified PDF text. That default action-taking pathway is more dangerous than medium because the blast radius can extend beyond a single document.
conditions: IF LangGraph routes pdf.js-extracted text directly into tool-using nodes
IF no verification step checks extracted facts before actions
mitigations: Require citation-backed verification before actions
Add a deny-by-default policy for tool execution
Show extracted text side-by-side with source PDF pages
Limit downstream actions to dry-run mode
requires-engineering: add policy gates before any external side effect

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and the profiles do not show a residency, certification, or retention mismatch. The only compliance-relevant data class is PDF documents flowing through LangGraph’s application-defined state, which could matter if those PDFs contain regulated data, but that is not established here. The other agent is not cited separately because no mismatch is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is embedded in the PDFs processed by pdf.js
IF LangGraph persists those PDFs beyond the intended retention window
mitigations: Define a retention limit for graph state
Avoid storing full PDFs in checkpoints
Classify PDFs before processing
Document data handling in operator runbooks
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
